thread:
maria: Heads-up — getting flapping SCIM provisioning for tenant `acme-inc`. Users created then immediately deactivated. Not seeing obvious Okta errors in the UI. Anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: saw a similar one last week. Usually it's either a duplicate group push or a race between SCIM deprovisioner and an automated RBAC backfill. What do the provisioner logs say?@jordan_s can you grab logs? :eyes:

jordan_s: grabbing now. quick snippet shows repeated: `PUT /scim/v2/Users/xxxxxxxx - 409 Conflict` followed by `POST /scim/v2/Users - 200` then shortly `PATCH /scim/v2/Users/xxxxxxxx - 403 Forbidden`.

maria: 403? that's new. Could be an auth between our SCIM service and KMS for decrypting extId. Any KMS errors in infra metrics?

alex_le: checking KMS logs — I see intermittent `Decrypt failed: KMS:NotFoundException` around the same timestamps. Might be a short alias rotation window. If extId is temporarily decrypt-failed, our provisioning flow marks user as invalid and deprovs.

sam: that matches. We recently rolled key alias swap in eu-west-1 on 1769998940. If the provisioner caches the old alias, there could be a brief window where requests fail, and retries end up creating duplicates.

jordan_s: dumping the exact request/response sequence (redacted):

```
PUT /scim/v2/Users/urn:okta:2:extid-12345
Request: { "active": true }
Response: 409 {"detail":"user exists"}
POST /scim/v2/Users
Request: { "externalId":"extid-12345" }
Response: 200 {"id":"u-abc"}
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/u-abc
Response: 403 {"error":"failed to decrypt externalId"}
```

maria: ok that's helpful. Two hypotheses: 1) KMS alias rotation caused decrypt errors -> transient deprovision; 2) Okta group sync is pushing assignments twice due to multitenant app config causing duplicate creates.

alex_le: to validate (#1) we can correlate KMS rotate times and provisioner error timestamps. Also check if decrypt failures correlate with a specific key version (I see logs referencing `arn:aws:kms:...:key/old-id`).

sam: for #2, check if the Okta app for acme-inc has both direct group push and SCIM group mapping enabled. That doubles create attempts. Quick check: in the app config panel for acme-inc, group push is enabled *and* an embedded group assignment rule exists.

jordan_s: I can disable group push briefly and run a test to reproduce. Would prefer to do a canary on staging first.

maria: yes run staging. Also add a temporary guard in the provisioner to treat Decrypt errors as retryable (with a short backoff) instead of immediate deprov. That will reduce user flip-flop during key rotations.

alex_le: agree. small PR idea: catch KMS NotFoundException and return 503 to caller so Okta SDK will retry instead of immediate deprov. I'll open PR and link it.

sam: also add an audit-log tag for attempts that hit key-rotation window. We need a clear trail for compliance: which tenant, request id, key_version. The console currently shows token-level traces but not key_version.

audit-bot: audit:scim_provisioner ERROR events=12 tenant=acme-inc first_seen=1769998895 last_seen=1769999010 request_ids=[rq-7ab, rq-7ac]

jordan_s: kicked off a staging repro now. disabling group-push for acme-inc -> repro rate dropped. staging run shows same KMS NotFound spikes at 1769998940-1769998960.

maria: recap action items:
1) alex to open patch to treat KMS NotFound as retryable short-term (PR + test)
2) sam to add key_version to provisioner audit events and console traces
3) jordan to run staged repro and post full redacted logs here
4) ops to schedule a safer alias rotation plan (rolling with overlap) for next rotation window

sam: I'll also add a Canary that runs an Okta group push sanity check post-rotation to detect double-assignment rules.

alex_le: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/provisioner/pulls/412 — adds retry on NotFound with 3 backoffs, adds key_version to audit events.

jordan_s: staging repro complete — attached trimmed logs in the thread (uploader) and ops confirmed rotation plan tweak scheduled for next maintenance window.

maria: thanks team. follow-ups in ticket: ENGSEC-4421. If anyone sees a customer impact spike ping me directly. :white_check_mark:
